newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude rises steeply on heating oil rally.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude rises steeply on heating oil rally.

text.p: NYMEX crude was swept into sharply higher territory Wednesday afternoon by a technically-driven heating oil rally, traders said.
"Heating oil is definitely leading the charge in crude, following plenty of buy stops," said Nationsbanc-CRT trader Dale Wong.
At 1430 EST, December heating oil was 2.75 cents a gallon higher at 71.00 cents. December crude was 63 cents higher at $23.98 a barrel. December gasoline was up 2.08 cents at 67.85 cents a gallon.
"The strength of the cash market combined with a technical breakout to create this rally," said a New York trader of the refined product strength.
Dealers noted buy stops were triggered in nearby heating oil after 70.15 cents and 70.50 cents to make a session high of 71.30 cents.
Nearby crude jumped after some stops were triggered near the $23.84 area, Monday's high in the front month.
Chartists said heating oil has emerged from an oversold condition in the 14-day Relative Strength Index.
But, Jake Bernstein, president of MBH Commodity Advisors, said heating oil has much further to rise before its technical picture became bullish longer term.
"We have had some good retracement, so this move was a little overdue," said Bernstein.
"Technically this does not change anything for heating oil. Heat would have to break 74.15, and there is still a lot of resistance until then," he said.
Heating oil revisted 50 percent retracement from its post-Gulf War high of 76.75 when it hurdled 70.50 cents, dealers said.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
